clue.text: Strengthen Aldi: on Tesco struggles

indicators.note: a supermarket that struggles is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A business pundit suggests the discounter Aldi should bolster its position while rival Tesco flounders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' signals the anagram of ALDIONTESCO; Aldi and Tesco are British supermarket chains.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate a position is to make it firmer and more secure, a direct synonym of strengthen.

clue.text: Correct my issue — good after work?

definitions.text: Correct my issue — good after work?

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an operation will fix their flaw and leave them looking good afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' signals the anagram of CORRECTMYISSUE plus G. Read whole, the clue describes the procedure itself: fixing a feature you dislike so you look good once the work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic operation corrects a perceived flaw in appearance, leaving the patient looking good once the work is done.

clue.text: Intelligence to grasp new words

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nous is common sense or practical intelligence

explanation.surface: Learning new vocabulary needs brains enough to take in fresh terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are a class of words, the naming words, so the plural fits words by example.

clue.text: Result revealed on show

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another means it comes first

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
to come is to show up or appear

explanation.surface: The winner of a contest is announced live on television.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the result or consequence of an event, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Losing wicket at the start, spoils period at the crease

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word
says the letter to go is the first one

parts.note: winnings are the spoils or proceeds of a victory or bet
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a team that loses an early wicket spoils its batting stint.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is where the batter stands; an innings is a batter's or team's turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an innings is the spell a batter or side spends batting, standing at the crease.

clue.text: Helping upset diva with heartless apology

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over into a new order
a heartless word has its central letter removed

parts.note: sorry is the word of apology

explanation.surface: A grudging sorry to an offended prima donna does little to help matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DIVA into ADVI; 'heartless' removes the middle R from SORRY, leaving SORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisory role is one of giving help through counsel, so the adjective matches helping as in a helping capacity.

clue.text: They ban kinky mum, sex actor and icon

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: Church authorities outlaw a racy trio: a mother, an adult-film performer and a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' signals the anagram of MUMSEXACTORICON; 'and' merely joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who excommunicate expel a person from the church, banning them from its sacraments.

clue.text: Stands when straddling bidet, having wiped bottom?

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A lavatorial picture: someone stands up after using a bidet and cleaning themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having wiped bottom' drops the last letter of 'bidet', the bottom in a down entry; 'straddling' wraps the word for 'when' round what is left. Bidet looks like a hidden word but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate it, just as one can stand or bear it.

clue.text: One's secure getting key

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
to land something is to secure it, as in landing a contract

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of a key and thereby feels safe.
explanation.walkthrough: A key (or cay) is a low island, especially in the Caribbean, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a small low-lying island or reef, as in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: See 22
Students — completely clean?

definitions.meaning: beginners or learners still being taught
read as two words, someone with ... is clean-living in every respect

explanation.surface: A question about whether newcomers are entirely free of bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into NO VICES, a person with no vices at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are beginners in a field, learners still being trained, so students in the broad sense.

clue.text: Change blue carpet

parts.note: to dress is to change clothes, as in dressing for dinner
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: A decorator advises replacing a blue floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is a verb here: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, as a boss calls an employee onto the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them severely, the same sense as giving them a dressing-down.

clue.text: Dance round mother's bra (without padding)

indicators.note: turning a word round reverses it

parts.note: MA is mother, so mother's is MA'S

indicators.note: padding is the filling in the middle, so the central letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A dancer swirls about in mother's unpadded bra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns mother's back to front; 'without padding' empties the middle letter out of 'bra'.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance, so the answer is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Steal piece

definitions.meaning: a steal is a bargain, something bought very cheaply
a small cut-off piece or clipping

explanation.definitionFit: A snip is both a bargain bought for very little and a small piece snipped off.

clue.text: Travels with strange duo on tour

indicators.note: a band on tour moves about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd pair of performers spend their time travelling on a concert tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tour' signals the anagram of STRANGEDUO; 'strange' looks like the indicator but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets around moves from place to place a great deal, an idiom for travelling.

clue.text: Awake, man on a toilet bent over making disturbance

indicators.note: in a down entry the man sits on top of the next piece, coming before it

parts.note: up means out of bed and awake
he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: bent over means folded back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: A man hunched over on the loo, wide awake, creates a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent over' reverses LAV to VAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or disruption, a direct synonym.

clue.text: State and prep schools initially fudged exams

indicators.note: something fudged is fiddled or botched, so these letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A scandal in which state and prep schools rigged their exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudged' signals the anagram of STATE, PREP and S, the first letter of 'schools' given by 'initially'. A prep school in Britain is a private school for younger pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Test papers are the sheets of questions sat in an examination, so they stand for exams.

clue.text: Plucks out, at last, name amongst sporting partners

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word before it
amongst places one piece within another

parts.note: WAGs, wives and girlfriends, are the partners of sports stars, especially footballers

explanation.surface: A tabloid story: a name is plucked from among footballers' girlfriends and finally outed.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is a British tabloid term for the wives and girlfriends of footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: To twang a string is to pluck it so it gives a sharp vibrating sound, as with a guitar.

clue.text: Before round, about to be drunk by piss artist

indicators.note: the swallowing combination comes before the next piece
one word drunk by another is swallowed, going inside it

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A boozer orders one more round, but first the piss artist drinks up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piss artist' is British slang for a heavy drinker; here 'artist' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Following pair of jumpers going over highest part of the building

indicators.note: the pair go over and around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: two kinds of jumper: a roo (kangaroo) and a top (sweater)
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Two athletes leap from one part of a structure onto its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pair of jumpers' is two different senses of jumper: a kangaroo, which leaps, and a sweater, as a British jumper is. 'going over' sets them either side of the abbreviation for following.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooftop is the outer top surface of a building, its uppermost part.

clue.text: Two times? Perfect

definitions.meaning: two units of time in abbreviated form, minute and time, written side by side

explanation.surface: A quizmaster checks whether doubling was the right answer, and is told it was spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: MIN is short for minute and T for time, two times run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in mint condition is in perfect, as-new state, as collectors describe coins and stamps.

clue.text: One believes he is only seen once in the robbery

indicators.note: the shared word appears once rather than twice, so one copy is removed

parts.note: a heist is a robbery, especially a daring one

explanation.surface: A detective is convinced a suspect appears only once in the robbery footage.
explanation.walkthrough: THE and HEIST overlap on HE: writing HE once joins them into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is a person who believes in a god, so one who believes.

clue.text: American and European's short match

indicators.note: short means a word lacking its last letter

parts.note: a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: A transatlantic sports fixture between an American and a European is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to correspond or tally, as figures agree when they are the same.

clue.text: Penguin to take one swimming about ice, lost chick briefly

indicators.note: swimming means moving about in the water, so these letters are churned into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of chick is dropped

explanation.surface: A penguin must dive in and swim around the ice floes to find its missing chick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' signals the anagram of ABOUT, ICE, LOST and CHIC ('chick' shortened by 'briefly'). Penguin is a British brand of chocolate-coated bar biscuit; 'to take one' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin is a brand of chocolate-covered biscuit bar sold in Britain, so it is an example.

clue.text: Outstanding score for other side securing victory

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: an own goal, OG, is a goal scored for the opposing side
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A football match report: an own goal gives the opponents a decisive winning goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owing is still unpaid, which is the outstanding sense of a bill or balance.

clue.text: European wine boxes for old England striker

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Graves is a red or white wine from the Bordeaux region

explanation.surface: A footballer of the past is gifted cases of continental wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Greaves was a prolific England and Tottenham centre-forward of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Greaves scored 44 goals for England in the 1960s, so he is the old striker meant.

clue.text: Right back with players and supporters

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: iPods are portable music players

explanation.surface: A football team's right-back appears alongside the players and the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' looks like the football position, but 'back' reverses RT to TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripods are three-legged stands that support cameras and telescopes, so they are supporters.

clue.text: The Sun will do this to newspaper numbers here?

definitions.text: The Sun will do this to newspaper numbers here?

parts.words: The Sun will do this to newspaper numbers here?
parts.note: sunlight discolours the sheets of an old newspaper, and the directory of business phone numbers bears that same description

explanation.surface: A query about what The Sun tabloid does to newspaper circulation figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way, sunlight turns old paper yellow; the directory of telephone numbers has that name. The Sun is also a British tabloid newspaper, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade telephone directory, printed on yellow paper, is where business phone numbers are listed.
